name: How the World Believes: A Tour of the Great Religions
description: From the fire altars of the Vedas to the newest world faiths: the beliefs, prophets and holy books that have shaped how billions of people live, pray and see their place in the world.

checkpoints.name: Roots of belief
checkpoints.note: Priests in India chant the hymns of the Vedas, Persian teachers speak of one wise god, and the Hebrew people shape their law and stories. These are the oldest strands of belief still alive today.

checkpoints.name: The age of teachers
checkpoints.note: In India, China and Greece, wandering teachers ask how to live well. The Buddha, Mahavira, Confucius and the Daoist writers set out paths of discipline and compassion that outlast the empires around them.

checkpoints.name: Faiths of the book
checkpoints.note: Christianity grows from a small Jewish sect into a religion of the Roman world, and then Islam arises in Arabia. Each is built on a holy book, and each spreads quickly along the roads of trade and conquest.

checkpoints.name: Spread and reform
checkpoints.note: Faiths cross borders and divide. Buddhism travels across Asia, Shinto takes shape beside it, Sikhism begins in the Punjab, and enslaved Africans in the Caribbean blend memory with new ritual to create Vodou.

checkpoints.name: New faiths of the modern age
checkpoints.note: Printing, migration and political change give rise to new movements such as the Bahá'í Faith and Rastafari, while old religions find new homes in every continent.
